records.title: 16 CFR 1632.31: Mattress labeling, records and the tag-removal rule
records.quote: No person, other than the ultimate consumer, shall remove or mutilate
records.note: Paragraph (b)(5). Paragraph (b)(3) requires the month and year of manufacture and the manufacturer's location on every mattress.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register)
records.title: 16 CFR 1633.12: Mattress labeling
records.quote: Name of the manufacturer
records.note: The same paragraph requires the complete physical address, month and year of manufacture, model identification and prototype number.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register)
records.title: 16 CFR 323.2: the FTC's Made in USA Labeling Rule
records.quote: all or virtually all ingredients or components of the product are made and sourced in the United States.
records.note: An unqualified "Made in USA" label needs final assembly or processing in the US, all significant processing in the US, and all or virtually all parts made and sourced in the US.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register)
records.title: 19 CFR 134.1(b): country of origin
records.quote: Further work or material added to an article in another country must effect a substantial transformation in order to render such other country the “country of origin” within the meaning of this part
records.note: US Customs' definition: the country of origin is where the article was made; work in a second country counts only if it substantially transforms it.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register)
records.title: 19 CFR 134.43(a): how imported knives must be marked
records.quote: shall be marked legibly and conspicuously by die stamping, cast-in-the-mold lettering, etching (acid or electrolytic), engraving, or by means of metal plates
records.note: US Customs' rule. Knives, forks, cleavers, shears, scissors, pliers and their parts must carry the country of origin by one of those permanent methods; goods of a USMCA country (Canada, Mexico) may use any reasonable method that is legible, conspicuous and permanent.

records.title: 19 U.S.C. 1304(a): marking of imported articles
records.quote: the English name of the country of origin of the article
records.note: Every article of foreign origin imported into the US must be marked, legibly and permanently, with its country of origin, unless an exception applies.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register)
records.title: 21 CFR 101.5: Food labeling, name and place of business

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register)
records.title: 7 CFR 56.36: Form of grademark and information required

records.title: 7 CFR 56.37: Lot marking of USDA-graded shell eggs (pack date)

records.publisher: ALDI Einkauf SE & Co. oHG (ALDI Nord)
records.title: ALDI Nord (aldi-nord.de), chronicle: the family shop in Essen, 1913
records.quote: Am 10. April 1913 nimmt Karl Albrecht senior in Essen-Schonnebeck den "Handel mit Backwaren" auf.
records.note: Karl Albrecht senior, a baker, starts a bakery-goods trade in Essen on 10 April 1913. He and Anna Albrecht are the parents of Karl and Theo, the founders of ALDI; after the Second World War the brothers take over the family business.

records.publisher: ALDI Einkauf SE & Co. oHG (ALDI Nord)
records.title: ALDI Nord (aldi-nord.de): the ALDI Nord group
records.quote: Die Unternehmensgruppe bietet Kunden in acht europäischen Ländern hochwertige Produkte zum niedrigst möglichen Preis
records.note: “The group offers customers in eight European countries …” Besides Germany, the page lists Belgium (since 1976), France (1988), Luxembourg (1991), the Netherlands (1973), Poland (2008), Portugal (2006) and Spain (2002). It lists no country outside Europe and doesn’t mention Trader Joe’s. Read in Chrome; the page is drawn by scripts.

records.publisher: ALDI Einkauf SE & Co. oHG (ALDI Nord)

records.note: From the chronicle’s list of countries ALDI Nord has entered since its first Dutch store in 1973: Belgium (1976), Denmark (1977–2023), Luxembourg (1991), France (1988), Spain (2002), Portugal (2006) and Poland (2008).

records.publisher: ALDI Einkauf SE & Co. oHG (ALDI Nord)
records.title: ALDI Nord (aldi-nord.de), chronicle: the name ALDI, 1962
records.quote: ab 1962 führen die Brüder ihre Diskontläden unter dem Namen ALDI
records.note: “From 1962 the brothers run their discount stores under the name ALDI.” Theo Albrecht opens the first ALDI Nord store in Dortmund that year.

records.publisher: ALDI Einkauf SE & Co. oHG (ALDI Nord)
records.title: ALDI Nord (aldi-nord.de), chronicle: the brothers divide the stores, 1961
records.quote: Die Brüder beschließen 1961, das bestehende Filialnetz unter sich aufzuteilen: Karl konzentrierte sich auf den südlichen, Theo auf den nördlichen Teil Deutschlands.
records.note: “In 1961 the brothers decide to divide the existing store network between them: Karl concentrated on the southern, Theo on the northern part of Germany.” The next sentence: “Despite the division, both companies work closely together.” The chronicle gives the rise of supermarkets and discounters as the background; it says nothing about cigarettes.

records.publisher: ALDI Einkauf SE & Co. oHG (ALDI Nord)

records.note: “Our group is connected to ALDI SÜD by family. As leading discounters in Germany we take own-brand harmonisation, marketing and important steps in sustainability together.”

records.quote: dont 60 % au minimum du coût de revient sont générés en Suisse

records.title: USPS Domestic Mail Manual 508.1.8: commercial mail receiving agencies
records.quote: A Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) is defined as a business that, in whole or in part, accepts the delivery of U.S. Mail on behalf of another person or entity as a business service.
records.note: A private mailbox at a store such as The UPS Store is run under these rules: the box holder fills in PS Form 1583, and the address carries a PMB number.

records.title: USPS Domestic Mail Manual 508.3.1: mailboxes are for mail with postage
records.quote: the receptacles described in 3.1.1 may be used only for matter bearing postage.
records.note: Section 3.1.1 makes every mailbox on a mail route an “authorized depository for mail” under 18 USC 1725. The only exceptions in 508.3.2 are for Sunday newspapers on rural routes and a separate newspaper box on the post.

records.title: 49 CFR 180.205(c): filling a cylinder that is due
records.quote: No cylinder may be filled with a hazardous material and offered for transportation in commerce unless that cylinder has been successfully requalified and marked in accordance with this subpart.
records.note: The rule that stops an overdue cylinder being refilled. The same paragraph says a cylinder may be requalified early, and one filled before its date may stay in service until it's empty. 2023 CFR edition.

records.title: 49 CFR 180.209(e): cylinders in non-corrosive gas service
records.quote: may be requalified by volumetric expansion testing every 12 years instead of every 5 years. As an alternative, the cylinder may be subjected to a proof pressure test at least two times the marked service pressure, but this latter type of test must be repeated every 10 years after expiration of the initial 12-year period.
records.note: Covers DOT 4B, 4BA, 4BW and 4E cylinders with a corrosion-resistant coating used only for non-corrosive gas, which is how grill and RV propane cylinders are made and used. 2023 CFR edition.

records.title: 49 CFR 180.209(g): external visual inspection
records.quote: When this inspection is used instead of hydrostatic testing, subsequent inspections are required at five-year intervals after the first inspection.
records.note: The visual inspection route; its table lists liquefied petroleum gas for DOT 4B, 4BA, 4BW and 4E cylinders. Inspections only by someone holding a current RIN.

records.title: 49 CFR 180.213(d): requalification markings
records.quote: must be marked with the RIN set in a square pattern, between the month and year of the requalification date.
records.note: The regulation's own example: a cylinder requalified in September 2006 by RIN A123 is stamped 9, the RIN in a square, 06, then the letter for the method.

records.title: First Alert: 10-year battery alarms
records.quote: Look at the manufacture date listed on the back of your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms and replace if they are 10-years old or older.
records.note: First Alert's US page, fetched once. It also says to replace an alarm at once if it doesn't test properly, and that some states require 10-year sealed battery alarms (it doesn't list them in the text we saved).

records.title: Kidde: end-of-life warnings on CO and combination alarms
records.quote: Since CO alarms cannot detect carbon monoxide in end-of-life mode, it's important to take precautionary steps when you realize your CO detector needs to be replaced.
records.note: Same page: an end-of-life alarm sounds every 30 seconds, digital ones show ERR or END, and a new battery won't stop it. On combination alarms Kidde says a chirp every 30 seconds is end of life or a sensor error, every 60 seconds a low battery.

records.title: Kidde: When should I replace my carbon monoxide alarm?
records.quote: As of 2013, all Kidde carbon monoxide alarms have a 10-year life, with the following exceptions: Model KN-COEG-3, KN-COPE-I, and KN-COPP-3. If your CO alarm was manufactured before 2013, it has a seven-year life.
records.note: Kidde's US support page, fetched once. It also says UL began requiring an end-of-life warning in 2009, and that Kidde recommends replacing smoke and heat alarms every ten years.

records.title: Kidde: How to tell when you need to refill your fire extinguisher
records.quote: If the needle on the pressure gauge of your fire extinguisher is in the green/full area, and the manufacture date is less than 12 years ago, your fire extinguisher is still good.
records.note: Kidde's US support page, fetched once.

records.title: Kidde: How to find the manufacture date on a fire extinguisher
records.quote: The bottom of the unit may have a two-digit or four-digit number stamped into the cylinder. The manufacture date may be printed directly on the cylinder.
records.note: Kidde's US help article, fetched once. Its worked example: 1205322062 = 12:05, day 322 (November 18), 06 = the year, 2 = the assembly line.

records.publisher: North Carolina Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Standards Division
records.title: NC Agriculture: RIN/VIN or Requalifier/Visual Identification Number
records.quote: If you want to requalify out-of-date cylinders, you need a Requalifier Identification Number (RIN) or Visual Identification Number (VIN). These are assigned by the USDOT.
records.note: North Carolina's LP-gas page, fetched once (last modified 25 Jul 2025). It points to PHMSA's locator to find a place that requalifies cylinders.

records.title: NFPA 10 (2025 edition), second draft report: 7.3.6.3
records.quote: Nonrechargeable fire extinguishers shall not be required to have a 6-year internal examination and shall not be hydrostatically tested but shall be removed from service at a maximum interval of 12 years from the date of manufacture.
records.note: NFPA's own public second draft report for the 2025 edition of NFPA 10, Standard for Portable Fire Extinguishers. California's fire code regulation (19 CCR 575.1) says the same in its own words.

records.title: NFPA 10 (2025 edition), second draft report: 7.3.6
records.quote: Every 6 years, stored-pressure fire extinguishers that require a 12-year hydrostatic test shall be emptied and subjected to the applicable internal and external examination procedures as detailed in the manufacturer's service manual and this standard.
records.note: The 6-year examination for rechargeable stored-pressure extinguishers, from the same report.

records.title: NFPA 10 (2025 edition), second draft report: A.3.4.2
records.quote: Nonrechargeable (nonrefillable) fire extinguishers are marked "Discharge and Dispose of After Any Use," "Discharge and Return to the Manufacturer After Any Use," or with a similar marking.
records.note: How the standard says to tell a disposable extinguisher from a rechargeable one: the wording on its label.

records.title: NFPA 72, Chapter 29 (household alarms): first draft report, 2025 cycle
records.quote: Smoke alarms shall not remain in service longer than 10 years from the date of manufacture unless otherwise provided by manufacturer's published instructions.
records.note: The 2022 edition's wording, shown in NFPA's first draft report for the 2025 edition (First Revision 5219, 29.11.1.4).

records.title: 27 CFR 5.66: who a US-made spirit's label must name
records.quote: If the name of the distiller appears on the label, it must be preceded by a phrase such as “distilled by,” followed by the name and address of the distiller.
records.note: The same section: a bottler is named after "bottled by", a processor after "produced by", "made by" or similar, and "produced by" on spirits means a processing step such as adding flavor, not distilling. The section covers spirits wholly made in the US with no imported spirits. The address can be the head office (principal place of business) instead of the plant, if the plant's address is coded on the label or bottle. "Bottled for" names the company the spirit was bottled for, which can be the distiller.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register)
records.title: 49 CFR 583.6: a supplier's part counts as all US/Canadian at 70%
records.quote: 100 percent U.S./Canadian, if 70 percent or more of its value is added in the United States and/or Canada
records.note: The parts-content rule for the window-sticker label (American Automobile Labeling Act). A part from an outside supplier counts in full once 70% of its value is added in the US or Canada; below that, its actual share rounded to the nearest 5%. So a car's filed figure can be higher than the share of value actually added in the two countries.

records.title: Fender support: dating amplifiers: how exact the charts are
records.quote: Although the dates derived using the charts below will likely be a good approximation, they should not be considered exact.
records.note: The same article defines Tweed, Brownface, Blackface, Silverface and Tolex, and says the face names come from the control panel's colour, not the grille cloth.

records.title: Fender support: dating amplifiers: transformer codes
records.quote: These numbers always begin with "EIA 606," and are followed by three or four digits in various combinations.
records.note: The same section: three digits means one for the year (7 is 1967), four means two (66 is 1966); the last two are the week, so EIA 606-4-21 is week 21 of 1964. Fender adds: allow about six months for time the parts spent in stock.

records.title: Fender support: dating amplifiers: speaker and pot codes, and the books Fender uses
records.quote: To use these books most effectively, you'll need to get the date codes from the speaker frames and potentiometers, and as much other detailed information as you can find about the specs and features of your amp.
records.note: The books Fender names: Fender Amps: The First 50 Years (Teagle and Sprung), The Fender Amp Book (Morrish) and The Tube Amp Book (Pittman). Fender says it uses them itself.

records.title: Fender support: dating amplifiers: the QA sticker date code (1990 on)
records.quote: All Fender amplifiers manufactured from 1990 to the present include a date code, printed on the quality assurance (QA) sticker on the back of the amp chassis.
records.note: The same section: the black-and-silver sticker has lines for sign-offs on sound and electrical testing; the last line holds two printed or handwritten letters, year then month, and "CE" means May 1992. Fender's year column runs from A (1990) to K (2000).

records.title: Fender support: dating amplifiers: why serial numbers don't date older amps
records.quote: While dating Fender amps made before 1994 by serial number is all but impossible (as records of these numbers were never kept), all hope is not lost
records.note: The same article goes on to three date codes that do work: the QA sticker, the tube chart stamp and transformer codes.

records.title: Fender support: dating amplifiers: the tube chart stamp (1951 to 1969)
records.quote: On the inside of the cabinets of most Fender amps made after 1950 and before 1970, there might be a "tube location" sticker.
records.note: The same section: the sticker may be rubber-stamped with two letters, year then month, in various positions; "JE" means May 1960. Fender's year column runs from A (1951) to S (1969).

records.title: Fender support: where the serial number is (amplifiers)
records.quote: The serial number on most Fender amplifiers can be found on the back of the cabinet or chassis.

records.title: Fender support: dating Indonesian-made instruments
records.quote: The serial numbering scheme for these instruments initially used the letters "IC" as a prefix indicating that they were made in Indonesia at the Cort factory.
records.note: The same article: Fender moved some Fender-branded production from Korea to Indonesia in 2008; from mid-2009 some use ICF. The first two digits are the year. Fender's chart stops at ICF11.

records.title: Fender support: dating Japanese-made instruments: Crafted in Japan and JD
records.quote: In 1997, Fender transitioned to a serial number decal that included the words "Crafted in Japan" above the serial number.
records.note: The same article: "Made in Japan" came back as a running change in 2007-2008, and from 2012 the serial is JD plus eight digits, the first two the year.

records.title: Fender support: dating Japanese-made instruments
records.quote: Records on early Japanese-made Fender instruments are not complete and are therefore not completely definitive for dating purposes.
records.note: Fender's Japan chart runs from JV (1982-1984) through single letters plus six digits to 1997.

records.title: Fender support: dating Korean-made instruments
records.quote: A "KC" prefix was introduced on Korean-made instruments in 1997, designating instrument made in Korea at the Cort factory.
records.note: The same article: Fender made Fender and Squier instruments in Korea from 1988, but its records start in mid-1993; serials with no letters (six to eight digits) begin with the year, so 98 at the start of eight digits is 1998.

records.title: Fender serial number lookup: the notice on the search page
records.quote: Please note that not all serial numbers are included in the lookup function for various reasons, however this is not indicative of any lack of authenticity.
records.note: Read in a browser on 16 Nov 2026; the search sits behind a CAPTCHA, so we read the page and did not search. Results show the serial, model number, description and a date.

records.title: Fender support: dating Mexican-made instruments: exceptions
records.quote: California Series electric guitars and basses from 1997 and 1998 use an "AMXN" prefix and share U.S./Mexico origin.
records.note: The same list: some artist models use MSN or MSZ, and two artist basses used MX before 2010.

records.title: Fender support: dating Mexican-made instruments: MX + eight digits
records.quote: This new scheme uses the letters "MX" as a prefix to designate an instrument made in Mexico, followed by an eight-digit number. The first two digits of the number identify the year of manufacture, (10 for 2010, 11 for 2011, etc.).
records.note: Fender's chart stops at MX17 (2017-2018); the rule is stated for the scheme.

records.title: Fender support: dating Mexican-made instruments: why each prefix spans two years
records.quote: necks that are made and serial numbered late in any given year are used on instruments assembled in the early months of the following year.
records.note: Fender's Mexico chart gives each prefix two years: MN8 is 1998-1999, MX15 is 2015-2016.

records.title: Fender support: dating Mexican-made instruments: MN and MZ
records.quote: Fender began producing instruments in its Ensenada, Mexico, factory in 1990. Instruments made between 1990 and 2000 carry "MN" prefix serial numbers, with the "M" designating Mexico and the "N" designating the 1990s.
records.note: Then MZ for the 2000s, and the same short-lived "10" scheme as US guitars from late 2009 to about March 2010.

records.title: Fender support: odd and non-standard serial numbers
records.quote: The "odd" serial numbers on the chart below exist somewhat outside the more well-known Fender serial number schemes.
records.note: The list includes DN (American Deluxe, 1998-1999), NC (Squier Strat Bullets, dating unclear), CN and VN (Korean-made, dating unclear), LE (1994), the SE, SN and SZ signature series, T (Tribute), C (Collectors) and XN.

records.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (filings written by the company)
records.title: Fender Musical Instruments Corp, Form S-1/A (9 Jul 2012): Japan
records.quote: we granted Kanda Shokai the exclusive right to distribute certain of our products, including Japanese-manufactured Fender products and Gretsch products, within the country of Japan.
records.note: The same paragraph: these deals followed the end of a joint venture in Japan with Kanda Shokai and Yamano Music, both then holders of more than 5% of Fender.

records.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (filings written by the company)
records.title: Fender Musical Instruments Corp, Form S-1/A (9 Jul 2012): outside makers
records.quote: We use approximately 97 OEMs as of April 1, 2012 to produce a significant majority of our fretted instruments, guitar amplifiers, percussion products and accessories. Our OEMs are primarily located in China, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.
records.note: The same filing: products made by OEMs were about 64% of gross sales in fiscal 2011, and are "typically sold at lower price points"; Fender makes its higher-priced products in the US.

records.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (filings written by the company)
records.title: Fender Musical Instruments Corp, Form S-1/A (9 Jul 2012): its factories
records.quote: We opened our Ensenada facility in 1987 and our current Corona facility in 1998. Our 176,000 square foot Corona facility and 167,000 square foot Ensenada facility manufacture guitars, guitar amplifiers and replacement parts.
records.note: Filed for a planned share sale in 2012. The same section: the Corona facility also houses the Custom Shop; the New Hartford, Connecticut facility primarily makes acoustic guitars; the filing lists manufacturing in Corona, New Hartford, Ensenada, Scottsdale (Arizona) and Ridgeland (South Carolina), and says US-made products are mainly the higher-priced ones; Fender leases all its facilities except Corona, which it owns.

records.title: Fender support: dating US-made instruments: the short-lived "10" serials
records.quote: These serial numbers did not identify the country of origin in the body of the number. Instead, the instrument's country of origin appears on the decal on the back of the headstock, near the serial number.
records.note: A "10", a space and seven digits, used from late 2009 to about March 2010.

records.title: Fender support: dating US-made instruments: N and Z prefixes
records.quote: The numbers and decals were produced far in advance, and some N9 decals (denoting 1999) were inadvertently affixed to some instruments in 1990. Consequently, some 1990 guitars bear 1999 "N9" serial numbers.
records.note: The same article: N marks the 1990s from 1990, Z the 2000s from 2000 (Z0 = 2000), and American Deluxe models add a D (DZ1, DZ2).

records.title: Fender support: dating US-made instruments: neck dates
records.quote: production dates have been penciled or stamped on the butt end of the heel of the neck of most guitars and basses, although there were periods when this was not consistently done (1973 to 1981, for example) or simply omitted.
records.note: The same article: a neck may have been made, stored and paired with a body the following year, so a neck date gives a range, not the build day.

records.title: Fender support: dating US-made instruments: why serials overlap
records.quote: due to Fender's modular production methods and often non-sequential serial numbering (usually overlapping two to four years from the early days of Fender to the mid-1980s), dating by serial number is not always precisely definitive.
records.note: Fender's two charts for 1950 to 1976 list each serial range with the year or years it was used; the ranges overlap.

records.title: Fender support: dating US-made instruments: S, E and V prefixes
records.quote: Serial numbers with an "S" prefix denote the 1970s (signifying a CBS attempt to use serial numbers to identify production years); an "E" prefix was introduced in 1979 to denote the 1980s. As seen in the overlap of numbers and years, even these references to actual production dates are rather loose.
records.note: The same article: V-prefix serials (US Vintage Series, from 1982) can only be dated from the neck heel. CBS sold Fender in March 1985.

records.title: Fender support: dating US-made instruments: US + eight digits
records.quote: This new scheme uses the letters "US" as a prefix to designate an instrument made in the United States, followed by an eight-digit number. The first two digits of the number identify the year of manufacture, (10 for 2010, 11 for 2011, etc.).
records.note: The same paragraph: the last six digits are not sequential and say nothing else; American Vintage and some special runs are exceptions. Fender's chart stops at US17, but the rule is stated for the scheme.

records.title: Fender support: dating US-made instruments: value
records.quote: Fender has no direct involvement in the used, collector or vintage instruments markets, and is therefore unable to comment or speculate on the current value of such instruments.
records.note: Fender points owners to vintage dealers and price guides instead.

records.title: Fender support: dating US-made instruments: where the serial is
records.quote: Serial numbers were stamped on the back vibrato cover plate on early '50s Stratocaster guitars, and on the bridge plate between the pickup and the saddles on some Telecaster guitars.
records.note: The sentence before it: serials have been on the top of the neck plate, the front or back of the headstock and the back of the neck near the body.

records.title: Fender support: where to find the serial number
records.quote: The serial number on most Fender guitars and basses is usually located on the back of the headstock or neckplate.

records.title: Fender Japan support: dating amplifiers (Japanese)
records.quote: 1990年から現在までに製造されたすべてのFenderアンプには、アンプシャーシの背面にある品質保証（QA）ステッカーに印刷された日付コードが含まれています。
records.note: Fender Japan's copy of the same article, with the same three charts: the QA year column also stops at K (2000).

records.title: Fender Japan support: dating Japanese-made models (in Japanese)
records.quote: 例：JD12xxxxxxであれば2012年製
records.note: Fender Japan's version of the chart gives the example JD12xxxxxx = made in 2012, and dates Made in Japan U + 6 digits 2010-2012 (the US page says 2010-2011).

records.title: Fender Japan support: serial number lookup
records.quote: Some of our modern products are sent directly from our factory to our distributor, without going through our database as well.
records.note: The same note: older and end-of-production items may be hard to find, and a used instrument may have been modified by a previous owner.

records.title: Ford distributor manual, Section 9400, page 7: warranty age
records.quote: Use the battery shipping date code to determine the age of the battery.
records.note: From the section on lost proof-of-purchase receipts. The customer must have the warranty sticker, its serial number must match the one on the battery cover, and any allowance goes toward a new Motorcraft battery. A warranty instruction to distributors. Page 8, effective October 2010, calls a battery new defective if it was never placed into service and is under six months old by that code. That is a warranty class, not a shelf limit.

records.title: Ford distributor manual, Section 9400, page 5: Shipping Date Codes
records.quote: Shipping Date is on a sticker placed on the side of the battery.
records.note: The drawing shows a round sticker reading C-2 and 3-2, each marked month and year. Ford pairs only C with 3 and doesn't print the whole letter list. Read on Delcoline's copy. The drawing also boxes GB1A58 on the top of the battery without saying what it marks.

records.title: Ford distributor manual, Section 9400, page 4: stock checks

records.note: A Ford-wide support page, not one model's manual. The archived link is the Internet Archive's copy of 2026-06-08.

records.title: Ford support: Tire Replacement

records.title: Fortune (Bloomberg), April 24, 2025: “Costco switched its Kirkland diapers and parents aren't happy”

records.quote: Compliance with the new and amended standards established for consumer water heaters in this final rule is required on and after May 6, 2029. … manufactured in, or imported into, the United States starting on May 6, 2029.
records.note: The standards cover heaters made or imported from that date. They don't apply to a heater already installed.

records.title: Energy Conservation Standards for Consumer Water Heaters, final rule (89 FR 37778): comment on lifetime (NMHC and NAA)
records.quote: NMHC and NAA noted that AHRI assumes a 10-13 year lifespan for water heaters, which is less than DOE's estimated lifetime.
records.note: NMHC and NAA are the apartment owners' associations; AHRI is the heating and water heater makers' trade group. DOE kept its own estimate.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register), via govinfo.gov
records.title: Energy Conservation Standards for Consumer Water Heaters, final rule (89 FR 37778): comment on lifetime (Bradford White)
records.quote: BWC noticed that the 2010 rulemaking reports an average lifetime of 13 years, rather than the assumed 15 years in the current rulemaking. … The assumed lifetime of 13 years for heat pump water heater products is also shared by the ENERGY STAR program in its materials that promote these products.
records.note: BWC is Bradford White. DOE answered that it had more evidence and a better survival curve than in 2010, and kept 15 years.

records.title: Energy Conservation Standards for Consumer Water Heaters, final rule (89 FR 37778): which electric tanks need heat pumps
records.quote: DOE anticipates a similar market shift in response to this final rule as the new standards for electric storage water heaters with capacities greater than or equal to 20 gallons and less than or equal to 55 gallons are met through the use of heat pump technology, while the standards for small electric storage water heaters (capacities greater than or equal to 20 gallons and less than or equal to 35 gallons) can be met by electric resistance heating technology.
records.note: Small electric storage water heaters are a separate class in the rule, defined by size and by how much hot water they deliver in the first hour.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register), via govinfo.gov

records.title: FTC press release, 19 Jan 1999: six makers settle Made in USA charges
records.quote: included the logo stating "Made in America by Honda."
records.note: The six were The Stanley Works (Husky and Proto mechanics tools stamped USA), American Honda (dealer ads for three lawn mower models), Kubota Tractor (T- and TG-Series lawn tractors "Made by Kubota in the U.S.A."), Johnson Worldwide Associates, USDrives and Rand International. The release also says the FTC kept the "all or virtually all" standard after its December 1997 policy review.

records.title: FTC press release, 17 Nov 2026: Elk River safety harnesses
records.quote: The FTC’s action against Elk River marks the fourth “Made in the USA” enforcement action taken by the Commission this year
records.note: The complaint alleges final assembly in Alabama but most components, including ones essential to the harnesses' safe operation, from outside the US. Proposed order: a $4.4 million judgment, suspended after $72,527 because of inability to pay. An allegation, not a court finding.

records.title: FTC case page: Kubota North America (2024)
records.quote: falsely labeling some of its replacement parts as being “Made in USA.”
records.note: Kubota agreed to a $2 million civil penalty, the case page says.

records.title: FTC case page: Oak Street Manufacturing (Oak Street Bootmakers), 2026
records.quote: FTC Announces “Made in the USA” Sweep, Including Three Law Enforcement Actions
records.note: Filed 14 Apr 2026 in the Northern District of Illinois against Oak Street Manufacturing Company, LLC, doing business as Oak Street Bootmakers; stipulated order entered 5 May 2026. The same sweep brought cases against Americana Liberty (flag poles) and TouchTunes Music. A stipulated order settles the case; it isn't a finding that the claims were false.

records.title: FTC case page: Williams-Sonoma (2024 civil penalty)
records.quote: civil penalty, which is the largest ever in a Made in USA case
records.note: Williams-Sonoma agreed to pay $3.175 million in 2024 for breaking a 2020 FTC order on its Made in USA claims; the complaint was filed by the Department of Justice on the FTC's referral.

records.title: FTC, Complying with the Made in USA Standard: "all or virtually all"
records.quote: the product should contain no — or negligible — foreign content
records.note: The FTC staff's business guide. It explains the 2021 Labeling Rule and the 1997 Made in USA Policy Statement, and says the guide is staff's view, not binding on the Commission.

records.title: FTC, Complying with the Made in USA Standard: Assembled in USA
records.quote: may be called “Assembled in USA” without qualification when its principal assembly takes place in the U.S. and the assembly is substantial
records.note: The guide adds that a simple "screwdriver" assembly of imported parts usually doesn't qualify, and gives a lawn mower with 15 to 20 percent foreign content as a fair "Assembled in USA" example.

records.title: FTC, Complying with the Made in USA Standard: brand names and flags
records.quote: Ordinarily, the FTC will not consider a manufacturer or marketer’s use of an American brand name or trademark by itself as a U.S. origin claim.
records.note: The same section says flags, US map outlines and references to US factories can imply a US-origin claim, depending on context.

records.title: FTC, Complying with the Made in USA Standard: cars and textiles have their own laws
records.quote: Under other specific laws, U.S. content must be disclosed on automobiles and on textile, wool, and fur products
records.note: The same guide: the Policy Statement and the Labeling Rule "apply to all products advertised or sold in the U.S., except for those specifically subject to country-of-origin labeling by other laws." For cars, that law is the American Automobile Labeling Act (49 USC 32304, 49 CFR 583).

records.title: FTC, Complying with the Made in USA Standard: civil penalties since the 2021 rule
records.quote: Marketers are now subject to civil penalties if they use an unqualified Made in USA label on a product that is not “all or virtually all” made in the U.S., including in catalogs or online.
records.note: The guide dates the rule to August 2021, when it was finalized; it was published in the Federal Register on July 14, 2021 (86 FR 37032).

records.title: FTC, Complying with the Made in USA Standard: qualified claims
records.quote: Examples of qualified Made in USA claims include “60% U.S. content,” “Made in USA of U.S. and imported parts,” and “Couch assembled in USA from Italian Leather and Mexican Frame.”
records.note: The guide warns that a qualified claim can still mislead: a treadmill with 3% US parts can't say "Made in USA of U.S. and Imported Parts", though "Made in U.S. from Imported Parts" or "Assembled in U.S.A." would be fine.

records.title: FTC, Complying with the Made in USA Standard: a cheap foreign part can still rule it out
records.quote: Because movements are essential to the watches’ function, an unqualified Made in USA claim is likely deceptive.
records.note: The guide's watch example: a Nevada-made watch with an inexpensive Swiss movement.

records.note: The same examples stood in every copy we read up to January 2021; today's guide drops them. Our decoder is tested against both.

records.publisher: Gibson (copies held by the Internet Archive)
records.title: Gibson serial guide, July 2012 copy: before 1975

records.note: The first PDF linked is gibson.com/Files/downloads/bluebook/GibsonSERIALNUMBERS.pdf, the Blue Book chapter we read for numbers before 1975.

records.title: Gibson serial guide: 2014 to mid-2019, no day of production
records.quote: These serial numbers do not indicate a specific day of production.
records.note: The same block: "It is not uncommon for a new model year model to be produced during the previous model year (example – a 2015 model may have been built in late 2014)." The format is YYRRRRRRR.

records.title: Gibson serial guide: back to the 2005 scheme in 2019
records.quote: In 2019, Gibson USA reverts back to its previous post-2005 scheme, which follows this pattern: YDDDYBRRR
records.note: Headed "Mid 2019-present Gibson USA". The January 2021 copy of Gibson's older guide page doesn't have this block: it still read "Gibson USA 2014 to present".

records.publisher: Gibson (copies held by the Internet Archive)
records.title: Gibson serial guide, January 2021 copy: "2014 to present"
records.quote: These serial numbers cannot be dated to a specific day of the year.
records.note: Headed "Gibson USA 2014 to present", with "YY is the model year". Today's guide ends that scheme in mid-2019 and calls YY "the production year". The 2018 and May 2019 copies read the same as January 2021; the 2012 and 2015 copies have no 2014 block.

records.title: Gibson serial guide: the eight-digit number from 1977
records.quote: 8-digit number impressed into the back of the headstock with "MADE IN USA" impressed below the number. The format is as follows: YDDDYRRR YY indicates the last two digits of the production year DDD indicates the day of the year RRR is the factory ranking/plant designation number.
records.note: The guide's heading for this scheme reads "1977-Present", and it applies to Gibson USA, Gibson Acoustic and Gibson Memphis.

records.title: Gibson serial guide: 1994 centennial numbers
records.quote: In 1994, Gibson's Centennial year, many instruments have a serial number that begins with "94" for the year, with the remaining 6 digits indicating the ranking number. These numbers, despite being 8 digits long, do not indicate the day of production.

records.title: Gibson serial guide: nine digits from July 2005
records.quote: Beginning in July 2005, Gibson USA moves to a 9-digit number, with the 6th digit now being a batch number. Batch 0 starts at the beginning of the day, and once we stamp 699, the batch number changes to 1.
records.note: The format: YDDDYBRRR, the year in the 1st and 5th digits, the day in the 2nd to 4th, then the batch and the ranking for that day. Gibson Acoustic, Memphis and Custom aren't in this change: it's Gibson USA's.

records.title: Gibson serial guide: artist models
records.quote: These models often deviate from the standard serial number format, and since many artists have multiple signature models across different brands, there are many different serial number configurations and variants.
records.note: Gibson asks owners to email service@gibson.com about artist models.

records.title: Gibson serial guide: banjos from 1988

records.title: Gibson serial guide: Custom carved tops

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register), via govinfo.gov
records.title: DOE central AC and heat pump direct final rule, 82 FR 1786 (6 Jan 2017): average lifetimes by region
records.note: Columns: national, North, hot-humid, hot-dry. DOE says units that run more hours each year (the hot-humid South) wear out sooner.

records.publisher: US Department of Energy, Appliance and Equipment Standards Program
records.title: Central AC and heat pump TSD (2016), chapter 9: why region changes the lifetime
records.quote: relatively longer lifetimes would be expected in regions with relatively shorter annual hours of operation, and vice versa.
records.note: DOE assumed half of failures follow hours of use and half follow age.

records.publisher: US Department of Energy, Appliance and Equipment Standards Program
records.title: Central AC and heat pump direct final rule TSD (Dec 2016), table 9.5.1: calibrated Weibull parameters
records.quote: Table 9.5.1 Calibrated Weibull Distribution Parameters … CAC 2 22.48 1 60 … HP 2 15.88 1 60
records.note: Shape, scale, a 1-year delay and a 60-year maximum for central air conditioners and heat pumps, fitted to shipments from 1983 to 2009. Our odds box uses these national curves.

records.publisher: US Department of Energy, Appliance and Equipment Standards Program
records.title: Consumer furnaces final rule TSD (2023), chapter 8: where the furnace curve comes from
records.quote: DOE then derived the Weibull distribution parameters for consumer furnace lifetimes by using stock and age data from U.S. Census's biennial American Housing Survey (AHS) from 1974-2021
records.note: The curve is fitted to decades of household surveys of furnace ages (AHS and RECS), not to any maker's figures.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register), via govinfo.gov
records.title: DOE consumer furnaces final rule, 88 FR 87502 (18 Dec 2023): average lifetime
records.quote: DOE estimates the average product lifetime to be 21.5 years for NWGFs and MHGFs. This estimate is consistent with the range of values identified in a literature review, which included values from 16 years to 23.6 years.
records.note: NWGF = non-weatherized gas furnace (the usual indoor furnace); MHGF = mobile home gas furnace. The rule gives 22.5 years in the North and 20.2 in the rest of the country.

records.publisher: US National Archives (Office of the Federal Register), via govinfo.gov
records.title: DOE consumer furnaces final rule (2023): heat pump lifetime used in that analysis
records.quote: Electric furnaces are estimated to have the same lifetime as NWGFs (21.5 years); however, heat pumps have an estimated average lifetime of 19 years.
records.note: A newer DOE figure for heat pumps than the 2016 AC and heat pump analysis (15.3 years), used in the furnace rule's switching analysis. DOE hasn't published a new heat pump curve with it.

records.publisher: US Department of Energy, Appliance and Equipment Standards Program
records.title: Consumer furnaces final rule TSD (2023), table 8.3.7: lifetime parameters
records.quote: Table 8.3.7 Lifetime Parameters for Non-Weatherized Gas Furnaces and Mobile Home … National 22.6 3.7 1.0 21.4 21.5 … North 23.9 3.7 1.0 22.5 22.6 … Rest of Country 21.2 3.7 1.0 20.2 20.2
records.note: DOE's survival curve for gas furnaces: Weibull scale (alpha), shape (beta) and a 1-year delay, with the mean and median it gives. Our odds box uses the national row.

records.title: Techtronic Industries, Annual Report 2025: Ryobi’s retail partners
records.quote: RYOBI continues to work with the best distribution partners in the industry, including the Home Depot in North America
records.note: The same report: “RYOBI is a registered trademark of Ryobi Limited, and is used under license.” TTI’s largest customer bought about 45.4% of its 2025 sales; the report doesn’t name it.

records.title: Unilever (unilever.com): Dove brand page
records.quote: Dove started life in 1957 in the US, with the revolutionary new beauty cleansing bar.
records.note: Read in Chrome; unilever.com refuses scripts, so the saved copy is our transcript of the page.

records.title: UPS Ground Saver page: PO Boxes
records.quote: UPS Ground Saver can deliver to U.S. PO Boxes, as well as APO, FPO, and DPO addresses, because eligible packages may be handed off to USPS for final delivery.
records.note: ups.com turns scripts away, so the page was read in a browser (Chrome) and its text saved.

records.title: UPS Ground Saver page: the new name for SurePost
records.quote: UPS Ground Saver is the updated name for the service formerly known as UPS SurePost.
records.note: ups.com turns scripts away, so the page was read in a browser (Chrome) and its text saved.

records.title: UPS Ground Saver page: tracking
records.quote: UPS Ground Saver shipments include end‑to‑end tracking using a UPS tracking number. Tracking updates are available while the package is in the UPS network, and delivery confirmation is provided once the package is delivered. When applicable, visibility may continue during final delivery handled by USPS.
records.note: ups.com turns scripts away, so the page was read in a browser (Chrome) and its text saved.

records.title: UPS Ground Saver page: who delivers
records.quote: Packages may be delivered by UPS or the USPS. Delivery photo confirmation only available for packages delivered by UPS.
records.note: The page also says Ground Saver is for “Customers with a UPS contract”, and takes 1 to 2 days longer than UPS Ground. ups.com turns scripts away, so the page was read in a browser (Chrome) and its text saved.

records.title: UPS Mail Innovations page: final delivery by the post
records.quote: we integrate with postal systems for final mile delivery
records.note: The page adds: “We handle functions—such as labeling and sorting qualified mail—normally done by USPS”, and calls the service a mailing services provider that picks up, processes and transports mail. ups.com turns scripts away, so the page was read in a browser (Chrome) and its text saved.

records.title: UPS Tracking Support: Mail Innovations tracking numbers
records.quote: Sequence Number (MMS/MMI Number): an 18-digit number assigned internally by UPS Mail Innovations or UPS Worldship
records.note: The same section lists a USPS Delivery Confirmation number (22 to 34 digits) and a shipper’s Compliant Package ID starting MI, then a 6-digit customer number. ups.com turns scripts away, so the page was read in a browser (Chrome) and its text saved.

records.title: UPS Tracking Support: a parcel marked delivered but not found
records.quote: If you still can’t find it, contact the seller to start a claim.
records.note: UPS’s advice for a package shown as delivered that can’t be found: check around the address and with neighbors first. ups.com turns scripts away, so the page was read in a browser (Chrome) and its text saved.

records.title: UPS Shipping Tools FAQ: shipping to a P.O. Box
records.quote: We only ship to a valid street address and do not deliver to P.O. boxes.
records.note: The answer goes on: packages addressed to P.O. Boxes “could be delayed, won’t be covered by any UPS Service Guarantee and will require an address correction charge”. ups.com turns scripts away, so the page was read in a browser (Chrome) and its text saved.

records.title: UPS Announces Significant Partnership Expansion with USPS (April 1, 2024)
records.quote: Following a transition period, UPS will become the USPS’s primary air cargo provider and move the majority of USPS air cargo in the US.
records.note: UPS investor relations, April 1, 2024: the contract was awarded by the Postal Service and took effect at once.

records.title: UPS Tracking Support: what UPS tracking numbers look like
records.quote: UPS tracking numbers appear in the following formats: 1Z9999999999999999 999999999999 T9999999999 999999999
records.note: Four formats: 1Z plus 16 characters, 12 digits, T plus 10 digits, and 9 digits. ups.com turns scripts away, so the page was read in a browser (Chrome) and its text saved.

records.title: The UPS Store: a UPS company, stores run by franchisees
records.quote: The UPS Store, Inc. is a UPS company.
records.note: The site’s footer goes on: The UPS Store locations “are independently owned and operated by franchisees of The UPS Store, Inc. (although one or more may be company-owned)”.

records.title: The UPS Store mailboxes FAQ: a street address, not a P.O. Box
records.quote: With a mailbox at The UPS Store, you get a real street address, not a P.O. Box number.

records.title: The UPS Store: USPS products and mailing services
records.quote: We offer USPS postage stamps, USPS Delivery Confirmation ® , Signature Confirmation ® and certified letters.
records.note: The same page lists Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express and First-Class Mail among the USPS services, and says to “visit The UPS Store® nearest to you” for them.

records.title: Reading U.S. Battery Mfg. Co. Date Codes (technical bulletin)
records.quote: written either in the format DDMMYY or YYMMDD
records.note: Flooded batteries use a month letter A to L, a year digit and a plant letter on the positive terminal.

records.title: 15 USC 45a: Made in USA labels
records.quote: with a "Made in the U.S.A." or "Made in America" label, or the equivalent thereof, in order to represent that such product was in whole or substantial part of domestic origin, such label shall be consistent with decisions and orders of the Federal Trade Commission
records.note: The 1994 law (Pub. L. 103-322) behind the FTC's labelling rule; govinfo's 2024 edition of the US Code.

records.title: 18 U.S.C. 1725: mailable matter without postage in a letter box
records.quote: deposits any mailable matter such as statements of accounts, circulars, sale bills, or other like matter, on which no postage has been paid, in any letter box
records.note: The offence needs “intent to avoid payment of lawful postage”, and the penalty is a fine.

records.publisher: US Congress (Office of the Law Revision Counsel); text served by Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute
records.title: 49 U.S.C. 30102: definitions (motor vehicle)
records.quote: “motor vehicle” means a vehicle driven or drawn by mechanical power and manufactured primarily for use on public streets, roads, and highways, but does not include a vehicle operated only on a rail line.

records.title: 39 U.S.C. 201: the United States Postal Service
records.quote: There is established, as an independent establishment of the executive branch of the Government of the United States, the United States Postal Service.
records.note: The law that set up the Postal Service in its present form, the Postal Reorganization Act of 1970 (Pub. L. 91-375).

records.title: 39 U.S.C. 202: Board of Governors
records.quote: The exercise of the power of the Postal Service shall be directed by a Board of Governors composed of 11 members
records.note: Nine Governors are appointed by the President, with the Senate’s consent.

records.title: 49 USC 32304: which vehicles get a parts-content label
records.quote: except that it includes any multi-purpose vehicle or light duty truck when that vehicle or truck is rated at not more than 8,500 pounds gross vehicle weight
records.note: The law behind NHTSA's yearly AALA reports, its definition of a passenger motor vehicle. A truck or van rated above 8,500 pounds isn't covered, so it has no row.

records.title: 42 U.S.C. 6295(b)(1): refrigerator and freezer limits from January 1, 1990
records.quote: manufactured on or after January 1, 1990: Energy Standards Equations
records.note: Set by the National Appliance Energy Conservation Act of 1987. Top-freezer, automatic defrost, no ice: 23.5 AV + 471 kWh a year; side-by-side with through-the-door ice: 30.9 AV + 547; chest freezers 14.8 AV + 223.

records.title: United States Postal Service, Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 (year to September 30, 2026): set up 1971 as an independent establishment
records.quote: began operations on July 1, 1971, succeeding the cabinet-level Post Office Department established in 1792
records.note: Item 1. The PDF posted on about.usps.com has “November 10, 2026 - Draft (6.0)” in its header, as the fiscal 2025 report’s had. records.title: USPS Publication 199, version 35 (July 2, 2026): what a USPS tracking number starts with
records.quote: Channel Application Identifier: 92, 93, and 94. The channel application identifier must always be included
records.note: Pub 199 is the Postal Service’s specification for its package barcode. Its Table 2 adds 95 for USPS retail counters and self-service kiosks. The example tracking number in the same section is 22 digits, and a scanned barcode adds 420 and the ZIP Code in front.

records.title: USPS Publication 199, version 35: the tracking number’s check digit
records.quote: The MOD 10 check digit is calculated using the following steps
records.note: The last digit of a USPS tracking number is worked out from the others, so a mistyped number usually fails the check.
